The user wants me to extract statements from the document according to a specific schema. I need to focus on statements about the partnerships' projects, money, perimeters, parties and states. The doc...I’ve reviewed the case studies on pages 36–43. They are comparative examples for Indonesia’s JETP context, so I’ll extract only the concrete statements about projects, money, parties, perimeters, and states that appear in them. I’ll treat each assertion as one line and keep the original wording where possible for classification.

Page 36  
- Vanuatu has approximately 300,000 residents spread across 83 islands. (count)  
- An estimated 30% of households in Vanuatu’s dispersed island communities lack electricity. (count)  
- The village of Loltong on Pentecost Island has a hybrid solar and hydropower mini grid that powers around 100 households, two schools, a clinic, several retail shops, and various community buildings. (named_item)  
- The Barrier Removal for Achieving the National Energy Road Map Targets of Vanuatu (BRANTV) has the objective of enabling the achievement of the energy access, sustainable energy and green growth targets in Vanuatu’s National Energy Road Map (NERM). (target)  
- The BRANTV project is supported by the Global Environment Facility (GEF). (funder)  
- The project builds on Vanuatu’s Off-Grid Renewable Energy (RE) and Energy Efficiency (EE) Promotion Program. (named_item)  
- The programme includes deploying RE-based power generation and distribution systems, primarily hydro and solar, as well as non-power RE applications such as solar-powered freezers for fishermen and solar fridges for cooperatives. (unnamed_item)  
- The programme also involves establishing the National Green Energy Fund (NGEF) to channel donor financing through grants or loans to RE and EE initiatives. (named_item)

Page 37  
- Donor initiatives to enhance rural energy access through renewable energy systems in Vanuatu have faced significant sustainability and replicability challenges. (event)  
- Many off-grid systems have failed over time due to inadequate funds for maintenance and limited local access to spare parts and repair services. (absence)  
- Vanuatu suffers from a shortage of skilled personnel to design, install and maintain off-grid RE systems. (absence)  
- There are few technical experts capable of managing village-scale systems and even fewer individuals trained to repair household-level photovoltaic (PV) systems. (count)  
- Public awareness of innovative RE technologies such as pico-hydro systems and energy-efficient (EE) stoves is also limited. (absence)  
- The country lacks robust policies, standards and enforcement mechanisms to support the development of RE and EE solutions. (absence) (absence)  
- There are no clear guidelines for implementing and maintaining village-scale RE systems or incentives to promote off-grid solutions. (absence)  
- The absence of a detailed roadmap for deploying systems across Vanuatu’s 2 000 villages hampers progress. (absence)  
- At the institutional level, barriers include insufficient management mechanisms to ensure long-term repair funds, lack of localized spare parts supply chains and limited government presence in rural areas. (absence)  
- Coordination between government departments regarding site identification and the productive use of RE technologies remains weak. (absence)  
- High upfront costs and a lack of accessible financing options also deter rural households and communities from adopting RE systems. (absence)  
- Financial institutions show little interest in extending loans and private sector investment in village-scale RE projects is almost non-existent. (absence)

Page 38  
- French renewable energy developer GreenYellow secured in 2023 a USD 13.8 million debt package to finance a rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) portfolio for commercial and industrial (C&I) customers in Vietnam. (event)  
- The portfolio includes up to 45 projects across Vietnam with a total peak capacity of 32.3 MWp. (quota)  
- Once operational the projects are expected to supply 31.5 GWh of clean electricity annually offsetting up to 15 530 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions each year. (target)  
- In September 2023 GreenYellow Smart Solutions secured a USD 13.8 million non-recourse project financing loan from four international lenders.
